problems.problem: The guard requires `request.httprequest.path` to start with `/web/dataset/call_button`, but §2.5 implements "Check for updates", "Update all", "Status", and the reconcile that runs when "Modules" is opened as `ir.actions.server`. Server actions are dispatched over `/web/action/run`, not `/web/dataset/call_button`, so every one of those entry points hits the guard and raises AccessError. The spec chose server actions deliberately ("list-header `display="always"` buttons in 19 are UNVERIFIED, so they are not used"), so this is not a stray detail — it is the primary UI path for check-for-updates, update-all and reconcile.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/addons/web/controllers/action.py:53 — `@route('/web/action/run', type='jsonrpc', auth="user")` then `action = request.env['ir.actions.server'].browse([action_id]); result = action.run()`. The only `call_button` route is /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/addons/web/controllers/dataset.py:34, reached solely by `<button type="object">`.
problems.fix: Either drop the literal path prefix check in favour of a set of allowed paths (`/web/dataset/call_button`, `/web/action/run`), or re-express every mutating store entry point as a `type="object"` button on a (transient) model and keep `ir.actions.server` for pure navigation. Whichever is chosen, add a test that exercises each menu entry end-to-end, because a path allowlist silently converts a working button into AccessError.

problems.problem: "One apply path: always restart … removes the mixed-code hazard (brief: T3)" and "New Python is imported only in the processes that exist after the restart" are false in prefork. Odoo 19's SIGHUP reload is a *graceful* reload that intentionally overlaps generations: the old master forks, the parent re-execs as the new master, and the forked child waits (up to 60 s) for the new master to signal readiness before stopping the old workers. With `-d <db>` set (the spec's own recommended shape, and the case preflight 12 treats as safe), the new master signals ready only *after* `preload_registries`, i.e. after the whole module upgrade has run — so for the entire duration of the migration the old workers are serving OLD Python against a schema that is being migrated under them. Without `-d`, the old workers are still alive while a new worker runs the upgrade on its first request. §2.9 H's user-facing text ("Users of prod will be disconnected for about a minute") is also wrong for prefork: they are not disconnected, they are served stale code.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/service/server.py:1175-1181 — `if server_phoenix: server_phoenix = False; self.fork_and_reload(); self.stop_workers_gracefully()`. :1105-1134 — `fork_and_reload` forks; parent `_reexec()`s; child installs `sighup_handler` and loops `while not phoenix_hatched and time.monotonic() < reload_timeout` (60 s) before returning. :1195-1209 — new master `run()` calls `preload_registries(preload)` FIRST and only then `os.kill(int(os.environ.pop('ODOO_READY_SIGHUP_PID')), signal.SIGHUP)`. :1136+ `stop_workers_gracefully` only then signals workers to "finish their current workload then stop".
problems.fix: Stop claiming T3 is eliminated. Either (a) make the prefork apply path stop the old generation before the new one migrates — which SIGHUP cannot do, so it means an operator-driven hard restart (`docker restart` / `systemctl restart`) for prefork, and the UI must say so; or (b) accept the overlap, document it, and add a guard that makes stale workers fail closed (e.g. hm_store models refuse to serve when `state.json.pending` names a serial that the running process's on-disk tree no longer matches). Re-scope S1(5)/S8(2) acceptance to measure the overlap window rather than assert it is zero.

problems.section: §2.4 HTTP surface + §2.9 H + S1(6) + Appendix B
problems.problem: The no-cookie status route cannot do the job it was invented for. It is the poll that *causes* the registry load: any request with a resolved `request.db` goes through `_serve_db`, which calls `Registry(db)` and therefore `Registry.new` if no registry is loaded. So (a) in prefork the first status poll after the restart runs the entire module upgrade inside a GET, subject to `limit_time_real`; (b) in threaded mode `Registry.new` is taken under a *class-level* RLock, so every other request thread — including the next 3-second poll — blocks for the whole upgrade, and those queued HTTP threads accrue runtime until `process_limit` adds them to `limits_reached_threads` and `run()` calls `self.reload()`, SIGHUP-ing the server *in the middle of the upgrade*. A 3 s poll cadence makes this self-inflicted restart materially more likely, not less.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/http.py:2849-2852 — `elif request.db: response = request._serve_db()`. http.py:2274-2277 — `registry = Registry(self.db)`. /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/orm/registry.py:99-106 — `__new__` does `with cls._lock: … return cls.new(db_name)`; registry.py:92 `_lock: threading.RLock`; `new` is additionally `@locked` (registry.py:115-117). service/server.py:509-524 `process_limit` adds any non-daemon http thread over `config['limit_time_real']` to `limits_reached_threads`; server.py:732-751 then calls `self.reload()`. tools/config.py:488 `limit_time_real` my_default=120.
problems.fix: Do not poll a db-bound Odoo route to observe a restart. Serve the phase from a file the reconcile/boot code writes into `<data_dir>/hm_store/` and expose it through a route that never resolves a database (no `X-Odoo-Database`, nodb routing), or poll a cheap static asset for liveness and only call a db route once, with a long timeout and no repeat. Back off the poll to a single in-flight request with exponential backoff regardless. Re-word §2.4's rationale and re-scope S1(6) to measure whether the poll triggers the upgrade rather than assuming it does not.

problems.problem: The reconcile table treats the presence of `base.partially_updated_database` as "Restart has not happened" and its absence plus pending module states as `stalled`. Both mappings are wrong, because `load_modules` re-inserts the flag at the end of a *successful* load whenever any module is still `to install`/`to upgrade`/`to remove`. So after a restart in which the load completed but a target did not reach `installed`, the flag is back and reconcile reports "Restart has not happened" and offers **Restart now** — which will re-run the same failing load, indefinitely. The two genuinely distinct outcomes (restart never happened vs. restart happened and the load left work pending) are indistinguishable from the flag alone.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/modules/loading.py:599-607 — `if update_module: cr.execute("INSERT INTO ir_config_parameter(key, value) SELECT 'base.partially_updated_database', '1' WHERE EXISTS(SELECT FROM ir_module_module WHERE state IN ('to upgrade','to install','to remove')) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING")`. Contrast orm/registry.py:172-176, where the DELETE is committed in its own transaction before `load_modules` runs.
problems.fix: Stop using the flag as the restart witness. Stamp a boot marker (process start time / a monotonically increasing boot counter written by the post-boot code) and compare it against `applied_at`: flag present AND no boot since `applied_at` = restart has not happened; flag present AND a boot since `applied_at` = the load ran and left work pending (`stalled`, offer the `--stop-after-init` CLI, never an automatic re-restart). Rebuild the §2.9 crash-window table and S1(8) acceptance on that marker.

problems.problem: The "workers and time limit" warning is gated on `config['workers'] > 0 and not config['db_name']`, i.e. it never fires in threaded mode. But `limit_time_real` is enforced on HTTP request threads in threaded mode too, and the consequence there is worse than a killed worker: the threaded server calls `self.reload()`, SIGHUP-ing and re-execing the whole process. A threaded server whose boot/first-request upgrade exceeds `limit_time_real` will restart itself mid-upgrade with no warning ever shown to the admin.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/service/server.py:503-524 — `process_limit` iterates `threading.enumerate()`, and for any non-daemon (or cron) thread with `start_time` compares `time.time() - thread.start_time` against `config['limit_time_real']`. server.py:732-751 — when `limit_reached_time` is set, `self.reload()` is called, which per server.py:764-765 is `os.kill(self.pid, signal.SIGHUP)`.
problems.fix: Drop the `workers > 0` condition; warn on `config['limit_time_real']` being below the threshold in every mode where the upgrade will run inside a request (i.e. whenever `db_name` is unset), and say explicitly in the threaded case that the server will re-exec itself rather than kill one worker.

problems.problem: "`hm.store.operation` … written through `sudo` only; `write()` and `unlink()` raise `UserError` unconditionally" is self-contradictory. `sudo()` only sets `env.su`; it does not bypass a model's own overridden `write()`. If `write()` raises unconditionally the state machine in §2.9 (operation → `applying` → `awaiting_restart` → `done`/`failed`/`stalled`, plus `applied_at`, `status_token_hash`, `error_code`, line `result`) cannot be written at all, by sudo or anyone.
problems.evidence: Spec §2.12 bullet 1 vs §2.9 B ("In a separate cursor … committed: operation `applying`"), §2.9 F ("operation `awaiting_restart` + `applied_at` + `status_token_hash`"), §2.11 ("marks `done`"). Odoo has no sudo-bypass of an overridden `write`: env.su is checked by `check_access` (/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/orm/environments.py:178-190 `is_superuser` == `self.su`), not by model method dispatch.
problems.fix: Define one explicit internal escape hatch and name it — e.g. `write()` raises unless `self.env.context.get('hm_store_internal')`, and every internal transition uses `with_context(hm_store_internal=True)`, exactly as §2.14's `hm_license_internal` already does for hm_license. State in §2.12 that the append-only `audit.log` and the server-side `odoo_store_events` are the sinks that survive a compromised in-database path, since the model itself cannot be truly immutable.

problems.problem: `odoo.service.db.list_dbs(force=True)` does not enumerate every database on the server. It returns only databases whose owner is the connecting PostgreSQL role, and when `db_name` is configured without a `dbfilter` it short-circuits and returns just the configured names. On the spec's own recommended shape (§1.5 step 4 sets `hm_store_database`, and `-d` is assumed throughout) a server running `prod` plus a `training` database owned by a different role, or simply a server started with `-d prod`, will report zero other databases. The `used_by_other_database` block and the restart confirmation that "names the databases whose users a restart disconnects" will both silently under-report, which is precisely the T10 blast-radius control.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/service/db.py:434-453 — `if not config['dbfilter'] and config['db_name']: return sorted(config['db_name'])`; otherwise `SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datdba=(SELECT usesysid FROM pg_user WHERE usename=current_user) AND NOT datistemplate AND datallowconn …`.
problems.fix: Query `pg_database` directly for all non-template, connectable databases (the store already opens its own connections via `odoo.sql_db.db_connect`), and treat a database it cannot connect to or read `ir_module_module` from as an explicit "unknown — could not check" row in the wizard rather than as "not affected". State the limitation in the restart acknowledgement text.

problems.problem: "`X-Odoo-Database` selects a database without a session" is only true when `db_filter` accepts that name for the request host. With a host-based `dbfilter` (the common multi-tenant nginx setup) or a `db_name` list that does not contain the store database, `dbname` stays None, the request is served nodb, and the status route has no database to read the operation from — it will 404 against the nodb routing map. Nothing in preflight checks that `db_filter([hm_store_database], host=<the host the admin uses>)` is true, and the failure only appears after Apply has committed, which is the worst moment. Separately, if the browser ever does send the session cookie, the header+cookie combination is a hard 403.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/http.py:1826-1839 — `if session.db and db_filter([session.db], host=host): … if header_dbname and header_dbname != dbname: raise werkzeug.exceptions.Forbidden("Cannot use both the session_id cookie and the x-odoo-database header.") elif header_dbname: session.can_save = False; if db_filter([header_dbname], host=host): dbname = header_dbname`. http.py:389 `def db_filter(dbs, host=None)`. http.py:2849-2856 — no db ⇒ `_serve_nodb`, whose router is `root.nodb_routing_map`.
problems.fix: Add a preflight check that actually performs the no-cookie GET against the status route before Apply is enabled (the spec already mandates a Test restart; fold this in as a Test status probe), and record the result on the operation. Make the client fall back to "Odoo is restarting…" on 404/403 from that route rather than presenting it as a store error.

problems.problem: `os.access(d, os.W_OK)` is evaluated with the process's real uid, and for a process running as root it returns True whatever the mode bits say. Invariant 6 and T23 both rest on "the operator's one command is the opt-in" — but on any deployment where the Odoo process runs as root (a `docker run` without `--user`, a hand-rolled compose file, a systemd unit without `User=`), preflight 5 goes green against the untouched 0500 directory and the operator never performs, and is never shown, the chmod. The one deliberate human gate on making addons writable is bypassed without anyone noticing.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/tools/config.py:1005-1017 creates the dir `os.makedirs(d, 0o500)` with the comment "will need manual +w to activate it". `os.access` uses the real uid/gid and root bypasses DAC mode checks; this container happens to run `uid=100(odoo)` (`docker exec hushmand-odoo id`), so the root case is UNVERIFIED here but follows from POSIX access(2) semantics.
problems.fix: Check the mode bits, not just `os.access`: require `stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(d).st_mode) & 0o200` on the owning uid AND refuse outright when `os.geteuid() == 0`, with a message telling the operator to run Odoo as a non-root user. Add the euid to the Status page and to `audit.log`.

problems.problem: An `auth='none'` route is given an Environment with `uid = None`. Calling `.sudo()` on that env sets `su=True` but leaves `uid` at None, so `env.user` is an empty `res.users` recordset and anything that touches the user (translations, company, `_compute` on a related field, any write) misbehaves or raises. The spec specifies the route's auth and response shape but never says how it obtains a usable environment to read `hm.store.operation` and compare `status_token_hash`.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/addons/base/models/ir_http.py:260-262 — `def _auth_method_none(cls): request.env = api.Environment(request.env.cr, None, request.env.context); request.env.transaction.default_env = request.env`. Contrast `_auth_method_public` (:265-268) which explicitly swaps in `base.public_user` when `request.env.uid is None`.
problems.fix: Specify `request.env(user=odoo.SUPERUSER_ID)` (or an explicit `with_user`) in the status controller before any ORM access, and make the route `readonly=True` so it takes a replica cursor and cannot write. Add it to S1(6)/S8 acceptance.

problems.problem: Preflight 8 hard-blocks the entire store whenever any `imported=True` module matching `^(hm|af)_` exists, but §7's row for it only promises "the specific message and its fix" and no fix is written anywhere in the spec. A customer who previously tried Apps > Import Module on a Hushmand zip — the exact thing the goal statement says they will have tried — is permanently locked out of the store with no documented recovery, and the blocking condition is invisible in the Apps UI because imported modules are filtered out of the load domain, not out of the list.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/addons/base_import_module/models/ir_module.py:38-39 — `imported = fields.Boolean(string="Imported Module")`; :50-52 — `def _get_modules_to_load_domain(self): return super()._get_modules_to_load_domain() + [('imported', '=', False)]`. Base domain is `[('state','=','installed')]` (/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/addons/base/models/ir_module.py:347-349).
problems.fix: Write the recovery path into §7 and into `docs/STORE-INSTALL.md`: uninstall the imported module through Apps, confirm the `ir.module.module` row is gone or `imported=False`, then re-run preflight. Add an S4 acceptance case that creates an `imported=True` hm_ row and checks the message names the module and the exact steps.

problems.problem: Three items listed as UNVERIFIED and used to gate slices are answerable from the container source and inflate the S1/S4/S9 gates: (a) `_register_hook` is explicitly documented and called during registry load, so S9's gating probe is largely settled; (b) `pg_dump` is present in the image, so preflight 15's hard-acknowledgement fallback is not the expected path; (c) the raw `ir_config_parameter` insert in `neutralize.sql` is valid as written. Treating settled facts as UNVERIFIED costs probe slices and, for S9, defers auto-rollback on a question that is already answered.
problems.evidence: /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/modules/loading.py:585-591 — "STEP 9: call _register_hook on every model. This is done *exactly once* when the registry is being loaded" followed by `for model in env.values(): model._register_hook()`. `docker exec hushmand-odoo which pg_dump` → `/usr/bin/pg_dump`; find_pg_tool at /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/tools/misc.py:153-160. `\d ir_config_parameter` on the live db: only `key` and `value` are NOT NULL, `id` defaults from `ir_config_parameter_id_seq`, and `ir_config_parameter_key_uniq` UNIQUE on (key) makes `ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE` valid.
problems.fix: Move these three out of Appendix B with the citations above. Keep an S9 probe only for the part that is genuinely open — whether a restored tree boots and whether exactly one further restart is emitted — not for whether `_register_hook` runs.

problems.section: §2.14 item 1 vs D13 (daily check cron) and §2.1 data/ir_cron_data.xml
problems.problem: `key = fields.Text(..., groups="base.group_system")` makes the licence key unreadable to any user outside `group_system`, including the user an `ir.cron` runs as. The spec's daily check cron re-verifies every `hm.license.key` and calls the catalogue endpoint with the licence envelope, but never says which user owns the cron. If it is left at the default cron user it will fail with AccessError on the first read; if it is set to a `group_system` user, that should be stated because it silently widens what the cron can do.
problems.evidence: Spec §2.14 item 1 and §2.3 `_store_verified_payloads()` ("Both decode from `key` every time"); §2.1 lists `data/ir_cron_data.xml` "one cron: check + notify only"; D13 "check-and-notify only". No `user_id` is specified anywhere. Field `groups=` enforcement is applied on read in the ORM regardless of cron context.
problems.fix: Specify the cron's `user_id` explicitly (`base.user_root` is the conventional choice for a data cron) and state in §2.12 that the cron's catalogue call is attributed to that user in `audit.log` and in `odoo_store_events`, so a daily outbound call is never mistaken for an admin action.

verdict: REJECT — four blockers, all verified against the Odoo 19 source in the hushmand-odoo container (19.0-20260817). The spec's overall shape (offline-signed code, verify-before-parse, swap-then-mark, restart-only apply) survives, but four load-bearing Odoo 19 claims do not. (1) §2.4's `/web/dataset/call_button` path guard rejects every mutating entry point §2.5 builds as an `ir.actions.server` — those dispatch over `/web/action/run` (web/controllers/action.py:53), so Check-for-updates, Update-all, Status and the reconcile on opening Modules all raise AccessError. (2) Invariant 3 is false in prefork: Odoo 19's SIGHUP reload deliberately overlaps generations — the forked child waits up to 60 s for the new master's ready signal before stopping old workers (server.py:1105-1134, 1175-1181), and with `-d` the new master signals ready only after `preload_registries` runs the whole upgrade (server.py:1195-1209), so old Python serves a migrating schema for the entire migration. (3) The no-cookie status route cannot observe a restart, because any request with a resolved db goes through `_serve_db` → `Registry(db)` → `Registry.new` under a class RLock (http.py:2849-2852, 2274-2277; registry.py:92, 99-106); in prefork the first poll runs the upgrade inside a GET under `limit_time_real`, and in threaded mode the queued 3-second polls accumulate until `process_limit` forces `self.reload()` mid-upgrade (server.py:509-524, 732-751). (4) §2.11's reconcile logic inverts on `loading.py:599-607`, which re-inserts `base.partially_updated_database` after a *successful* load that left modules pending — so "flag present ⇒ restart has not happened" is wrong and its **Restart now** button loops. Beyond those: preflight 12 excludes threaded mode from the time-limit warning although threaded enforcement re-execs the whole server; §2.12's unconditionally-raising `write()` contradicts the sudo-written state machine with no escape hatch defined; `list_dbs` under-reports other databases (T10); no preflight proves `db_filter` accepts the store database for the admin's host; and `os.access(W_OK)` passes for root, silently bypassing the operator opt-in that invariant 6 and T23 rest on. Verified-and-sound, worth keeping as written: addons_data_dir creation at 0500 and its position ahead of every `addons_path` entry (config.py:1005-1017, module.py:140-152); `Manifest._get_manifest_from_addons` being an uncleaned `lru_cache` with a reachable `cache_clear` while `all_addon_manifests()` re-lists directories (module.py:278-281, 317-330); `Registry.new`'s committed flag DELETE and `update_module=True` (registry.py:163-176); STEP 3 loading `to install` modules (loading.py:450-467); `button_upgrade` calling `update_list()` and `button_install`ing new dependencies (ir_module.py:704-752); `assert_log_admin_access` requiring `env.is_admin()` and `group_system` implying `group_erp_manager` (ir_module.py:57-73, environments.py:182-190, base_groups.xml:35-40); `check_identity` refusing without a request and re-prompting after 10 minutes (res_users.py:87-126); CSRF applying only to non-safe methods (http.py:225, 2493); `restart()` as SIGHUP to `server.pid` with `os.execve` preserving PID 1 (server.py:1526-1544, 1681-1688); the `--dev=reload` watcher gate and its recursive watch of every addons path, which is why preflight 3 must block it (server.py:333-339, 1657); unknown `odoo.conf` keys stored as-is and readable via `config.get()` (config.py:901-917, 981-982); and neutralize running `<module>/data/neutralize.sql` for installed modules (modules/neutralize.py:27-40). Docker was down at session start; I started Docker Desktop and read everything above in the live `hushmand-odoo` container, so nothing in this review is asserted from memory.
